title: flow-tiles-ux-sandbox
body:
Context:
This is a rough personal scratchpad for a small feature experiment: "flow tiles" — a visual, tile-based UI for composing short conversational microflows (snippets of prompt + routing + post-processing) that product teams can assemble quickly and run against Redwood deployments. The idea is midway between Prompts-as-Templates and a full composer: lighter than a flow-graph, heavier than a single prompt editor.

Why this?
- Customers routinely want reusable subroutines (summary + citation, extract entities then rerank, multi-step clarification) 
- Current UX: single prompt box or full orchestration infra. There’s a gap for non-engineer builders and quick prototyping.
- Should lower friction to try different routing/cost options (hosted vs dedicated), preview token costs, and compose repeatable building blocks.

High level goal:
Create a lightweight, drag-to-assemble tile UI that:
- captures common microflows as first-class objects (tile types: prompt, transform, rerank, call-tool, embed-match, conditional)
- shows estimated token/cost impact per tile and end-to-end
- can be run in a sandbox mode against a dev key (hosted) or point to Dedicated/Private endpoints for accuracy tests
- exports JSON that backend can interpret as a compact execution graph (linear + simple branches)

Success metrics (initial):
- 40% of early adopters in internal beta use tiles for >1 workflow within two weeks
- Median time to assemble + run a microflow < 6 minutes for first-time users
- 25% reduction in average tokens used vs naive monolithic prompt for the same task (through explicit extract/condense tiles)

Personas:
- PM / non-ML product builder: wants to prototype an assistant behavior without engineering hours
- ML/Infra engineer: wants a way to package and version micro-ops for reuse across products
- Solutions engineer / customer success: compose demos quickly, toggle model/routing to show cost/latency tradeoffs

Draft user stories (prioritized):
1) As a PM, I can drag a "Summarize" tile and type a short instruction, connect it to an "Embed" tile, and run the assembled flow against a test conversation so I can see output + token estimate.
2) As an engineer, I can attach a tile-level routing override (dedicated:gpu-a → quantized model v2) so I can measure latency difference for that tile.
3) As a solutions engineer, I can save a tile group as a reusable "macro" and share link with a colleague.
4) As a PM, I can preview per-tile cost breakdown and an overall SLO/latency estimate before running.
5) As an infra lead, I can export the flow as compact JSON that maps to existing runtime ops (prompt -> model call, embed -> embedding endpoint, rerank -> candidate rerank).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Drag-and-drop canvas with at least 5 tile types implemented (prompt, embed, rerank, conditional, tool-call)
- Execution sandbox that runs in-hosted mode and returns outputs within token/latency bounds for demo datasets
- Per-tile token estimate algorithm: simple heuristic (tokens in prompt + expected output tokens default) with a visible margin
- Save/load flows persisted to user's Drive area (or prototype storage), plus shareable URL (token-protected)
- Exported JSON schema v0 that backend engineers can map to a real executor (flat list with sequence and optional branch conditions)

Design notes / UX heuristics:
- Keep tiles compact: title, small instruction line, tiny icon for tile type, cost badge (est. tokens / est. $)
- Hover preview expands to show sample output and the raw prompt template (editable)
- Connections are directional lines; limit branching depth to avoid building a full dataflow graph in MVP
- Allow quick model switch per-tile with presets: fast/cheap, balanced, high-fidelity; each preset maps to a known model id + quantization config
- Provide a "simulate" mode that runs with mocked latency/cost using historical stats to avoid heavy infra use during early prototyping

Backend spike (engineering checklist):
- schema-v0: flat array of {id, type, instruction, params, routing_hint, next_id[], branch_condition?} (this is text-only proposal; need to align with runtime team)
- lightweight interpreter service for sandbox that translates schema-v0 to sequential API calls with KV carrying (tokenize intermediate outputs as needed)
- token estimation service: reuse existing tokenization libs + historical multipliers per model family
- permissions: flows saved under user; shareable links with read-only / edit flags; integrate with Drive metadata later

Experiment plan / A/B ideas:
- A: show explicit per-tile cost badges vs B: only show end-to-end cost; measure whether badges reduce token usage in subsequent edits
- B1: allow one-click convert-to-monolithic prompt (flatten tiles) to compare quality/cost; measure preference
- Early PD: limited to internal set of templates (summary, extract, transform) to collect telemetry on tile combinations

Telemetry & metrics to capture:
- Tile usage frequency (which tile types become dominant)
- Flow length distribution (#tiles per flow)
- Token consumption per tile & per flow, model selection distribution
- Time-to-first-successful-run per user
- Share rate (how often flows are shared externally)

Open questions / risks:
- When branching, how to represent state and KV cache? (do we snapshot intermediate transcripts?)
- Security: tool-call tiles could become an injection vector; need input sanitization + execution sandboxing
- Complexity creep: users may start building complex DAGs — we should intentionally cap features in MVP and add a "full graph" product later
- Pricing UX: showing cost estimates publicly could be sticky if estimates are inaccurate. Start with conservative high-margin estimates and label clearly as "estimate"

Next steps (short term):
- Run a 1-week internal design sprint with 1 engineer + 1 designer + 1 PM (Priya volunteered) to produce clickable Figma and a repo scaffold
- Spike token estimation and schema mapping (Aiden)
- Prepare 3 demo flows for internal beta (support agent demo, docs summarizer, entity extraction + rerank)
- Sync with runtime owners (Serving Runtime team) to validate schema pairing and cost estimation signals (tag meeting request in Slack)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first UX linear and conservative; avoid making this a low-friction way to shoot compute at huge datasets
- Think about "templates marketplace" as a future GTM angle for Solutions Engineers to publish polished tile sets
- Could be an entry point to Redwood Optimize: show recommendations (batching on/off, quantize suggestion) per tile

References / inspiration:
- notion of "blocks" (Notion), low-code flow UIs (Zapier), but with token/cost-first constraints
- internal convo: see Slack thread (link above) where someone prototyped a 3-tile reuse for summarization

End of scratchpad — will iterate after the internal sprint outputs and any early telemetry.
